Plant_Material: Endophyte FL0768 was isolated from healthy, surface-sterilized photosynthetic tissue of a freshly collected stem of the sand spikemoss (Selaginella arenicola) obtained from a pine-dominated forest in central Florida, USA.
Fermentation_Condition: A culture of Anteaglonium sp. FL0768 grown on PDA for 2 weeks was used for extraction. The culture media and mycelium from 13 T-flasks (800 mL), each containing 135 mL of PDA coated on five sides of the flasks, maximizing the surface area for fungal growth (total surface area/flask ca. 460 cm2), were extracted with MeOH (3.2 L) in an ultrasonic bath for 1 h.

Fermentation_Condition: The strain Penicillium sclerotiorum ZJHJJ-18 was inoculated on PDA plates at room temperature for 5 days. Plant_Material: The almonds of Bertholletia excelsa were collected and assigned by the Brazilian Agricultural Research Corporation—Amapá, Brazil, in the area located 1—W 52° 18′ 20.976″ and S 0° 33′ 44.44″ and 2—W 51° 57′ 53.338″ and S 0° 25′ 21.39″ (Amapá State, Brazil).
Fermentation_Condition: The strain of the endophytic fungus was grown in a solid culture medium PDA (potato-dextrose-agar), then the material was sterilized in an autoclave (Phoenix, AV50) at 121 °C for 20 min then the sterile medium was poured into plates Petri 90 mm. After 24 h, the petri dishes containing culture medium PDA were inoculated with spores of the fungus Aspergillus sp. using an inoculation needle through a central insertion point, the strain was then incubated at 28 °C (DBO, LACADEMA, model LUCA-161/03) as described by (Holanda et al. 2019) during the 7-day period. Next, inoculations were performed with four circular discs (0.5 cm in diameter) from a solid culture in five different 500 mL Erlenmeyers flasks, each containing 200 mL of liquid culture medium malt (2%) at pH 7.0. Each Erlenmeyer flask was incubated for 10 days in standard weather conditions with a temperature 28 °C ± 2 °C and 160 rpm. The growth of the mycelial mass in liquid medium was performed in quintuplicate.

The resulting seed culture was adjusted to McFarland standard (1 × 106 CFU/mL) and about 200 μL was then transferred into a flask (1000 mL) containing 500 mL of the same production medium. It was then incubated for 10 days at 28 °C under agitation at 150 rpm.

The resulting seed culture was adjusted to McFarland standard (1 × 106 CFU/mL) and about 200 μL was then transferred into a flask (1000 mL) containing 500 mL of the same production medium. It was then incubated for 10 days at 28 °C under agitation at 150 rpm.

The resulting seed culture was adjusted to McFarland standard (1 × 106 CFU/mL) and about 200 μL was then transferred into a flask (1000 mL) containing 500 mL of the same production medium. It was then incubated for 10 days at 28 °C under agitation at 150 rpm.

Plant_Material: Red ginseng was bought from the Juhuacuen Chinese medicinal material of Kunming in Yunnan Province in People's Republic of China. The fungus Aspergillus tubingensis S1120 isolated from the leaves of Dendrobium officinale (denoff-6) was collected from Wenshan of Yunnan Province in People′s Republic of China.
Fermentation_Condition: The A. tubingensis S1120 was fermented on the medium of potato dextrose agar (PDA) (200 g of potato, 18 g of agar and 20 g of sucrose in 1 L water) at 28 °C for three days. Mycelia of PDA medium were inoculated into 0.5 L Erlenmeyer flasks of PDB medium (200 g of potato, 20 g of sucrose, and 1 L of water) at 28 °C and 160 rpm for 2 days. The PDB fermentation broths were cocultured with the red ginseng (7 kg) for 45 days at 28 °C.

Plant_Material: The fungus Alternaria sp. J030 was isolated from the leaves of Bauhinia variegata Linn. var. candida (Roxb.) Voigt, which was collected from Zhaoqing City, Guangdong Province, P. R. China, in October 2021.
Fermentation_Condition: Alternaria sp. J030 was cultured on potato dextrose agar for 5 days at 28 °C to prepare the seed culture. Agar plates, including the strain, were cut into small pieces, then these pieces were inoculated into 400 Erlenmeyer flasks (350 mL), previously sterilized by autoclaving, each containing 40 g of rice and 35 mL of distilled water. All flasks were incubated at 28 °C for 30 days.

Plant_Material: The fungal strain LSLYZ-87 used in this study was obtained from the fresh leaves of marine mangrove Acanthus ilicifolius L, gathered in March 2019 from the Huizhou Mangrove National Nature Reserve in Guangdong Province, China.
Fermentation_Condition: The fungus Phomopsis asparagi LSLYZ-87 was activated and cultured in shaker on potato dextrose broth (PDB) to obtain spore inoculum for a week at 28 °C (4×500 mL-Erlenmeyer flasks). The routine-scale fermentation was carried out in 30×1 L-Erlenmeyer flasks, each consisting of 100 mL of potato juice, 2 g of sea salt (2 % saline), 0.5 g of peptone and 2 g of sucrose. The Erlenmeyer flask containing the culture medium was autoclaved at 121 °C for 25 min. Then, 20 mL of inoculum was inoculated in each bottle after cooling, and incubated for 30 days at room temperature.

The flasks were cultivated in rotary shaker with 180 rpm at 25 °C for three days to get the seed cultures. And then, the seeds were inoculated to 25×1 L Erlenmeyer flasks, each containing 130 g millet, 0.2 g bacterial peptone, and 160 mL sea water. After inoculation, these flasks were cultivated in 25 °C under static condition.

Plant_Material: The strain C. rhizophorae Kohlm. & E. Kohlm (Valsaceae) was isolated from the plant Gynochthodes officinalis (F.C. How) Razafim. & B. Bremer (Rubiaceae), which was collected from Gaoyao city of Guangdong province in January 2015.
Fermentation_Condition: The strain of C. rhizophorae A761 was cultured in potato dextrose broth (potato 20%, glucose 2%, K2HPO4 0.3%, MgSO4•7H2O 0.15%, vitamin B 10 mg/L). The fungus C. rhizophorae A761 was maintained on potato dextrose agar (PDA) medium at 28 °C for 5 days, and then three pieces (0.5 × 0.5 cm2) of mycelial agar plugs were inoculated into 20 × 500 mL Erlenmeyer flasks, each containing 250 mL potato dextrose broth. After 4 days of incubation at 28 °C on a rotary shaker at 120 r/m, 25 mL seed cultures were aseptically transferred into the rice solid medium (each flask contained 300 g of rice, 380 mL of natural filtered water). The 17 flasks (3000 mL) were then kept for 30 days at 28 °C.

Plant_Material: The health and fresh kiwi plants and kiwifruits were collected from Guanyuan City, Sichuan Province, People's Republic of China. All endophytic fungi were obtained simultaneously from at least three different healthy tissues.
Fermentation_Condition: The strains were cultured in PDA and stored at −4 °C. Culture medium was composed of pork peptone (0.15%), yeast (0.15%), glucose (5%), KH2PO4 (0.05%) and MgSO4 (0.05%). Initial pH was adjusted to 7.0, the fermentation was first carried out on an erlenmeyer flask for 4 days till the mycelium biomass reached to the maximum. Then it was transferred to rice medium at 25 °C in dark culture for 60 days. The rice medium in each 250 mL-Erlenmeyer flask was composed of rice (50 g) and water (50 mL). A total of 300 bottles were used in this research.

Plant_Material: Healthy leaf samples of Albizia lucidior (Steud.) I.C. Nielsen were collected from the Zoological garden, Giza, Egypt, in March 2019.
Fermentation_Condition: To prepare the fungal seed culture, the endophytic strain was sub-cultured on potato dextrose agar medium plate at 28 °C for five days. Six agar plugs (0.5 × 0.5 cm2) with mycelia were inoculated into 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask, containing 50 mL potato dextrose broth liquid media (PDB) and incubated at 28 °C in a shaker incubator at 180 rpm for two days. An aliquot (5 mL) of fungal seed culture was transferred to 5 × 1 L Erlenmeyer flasks, each one containing 250 mL of PDB and incubated for 15 days under the same conditions of the seed culture.

Plant_Material: The endophytic fungi were isolated from fresh and healthy stems of kiwi plant (Actinidia chinensis Planch. Actinidiaceae) which collected from Cangxi county of Sichuan Province (GPS: N 31°12′, E 105°76′) in July 2018.
Fermentation_Condition: This strain was cultured on potato dextrose agar (PDA) medium at 24 °C for 10 days, and then was cut into small pieces to incubate on solid rice medium. The rice medium was inoculated in 500-mL Erlenmeyer flasks, each containing 100 g of rice medium and 100 mL of water. Flask cultures were put into a high-pressure sterilizing pot and sterilized at 121 °C for 15 min. Then, the strain of P. sporulosa was cultured in the rice medium. A total of 200 flasks were incubated fixedly at 25 °C for 30 days in dark place.

Fermentation_Condition: The endophytic fungus Xylaria sp. was cultured on potato dextrose agar (PDA) at 25 °C for 15 days. Finally, seed broth (25 mL) was added to sixty 500-mL conical ﬂasks, each containing 80 g of rice and 120 mL of distilled H2O after autoclaving at 120 °C for 30 min, and these flasks were incubated statically at room temperature for 70 days.

Plant_Material: Emericella sp. Berk (Trichocomaceae) strain XL029 was obtained from the leaves of Panax notoginseng (Burkill) F.H.Chen ex C.Y.Wu & K.M.Feng (Araliaceae) collected from Shijiazhuang (east longitude 114°30′08.9″, north latitude 38°2′43.7″), Hebei Province, P. R. China, in September 2015 with dry autumn.
Fermentation_Condition: The fungal strain Emericella sp. XL029 was cultivated on potato dextrose agar (PDA) at 28 °C for 5 days. Then, the pure cultures were cut into small pieces, transferred into 500 mL flasks containing 300 mL of PDB medium, and incubated at 160 rpm and 28 °C for 5 days to obtain the seed culture. Large-scale culture was performed in 150 flasks (500 mL), and each flask contained 80 g of rice plus 80 mL of wheat bran liquid medium (2.0% glucose, 0.3% potassium dihydrogen phosphate, 0.15% magnesium sulfate heptahydrate, and 3.0% wheat bran, which was boiled for 30 min and strained, and the final pH of the medium was adjusted to 6.0 before sterilization) and inoculated with 10 mL of the seed culture. After cultivation at room temperature for 50 days, fermented cultures from 150 flasks were harvested for chemical study.

Large-scale culture was performed in 150 flasks (500 mL), and each flask contained 80 g of rice plus 80 mL of wheat bran liquid medium (2.0% glucose, 0.3% potassium dihydrogen phosphate, 0.15% magnesium sulfate heptahydrate, and 3.0% wheat bran, which was boiled for 30 min and strained, and the final pH of the medium was adjusted to 6.0 before sterilization) and inoculated with 10 mL of the seed culture. After cultivation at room temperature for 50 days, fermented cultures from 150 flasks were harvested for chemical study.

Plant_Material: The strain SC-J0123 of Diaporthe ueckerae Udayanga & Castl (Diaporthaceae), was isolated from the leaf of Pteris vittate L. (Pteridaceae) collected from Shatoujiao forestry center, Guangdong, People's Republic of China.
Fermentation_Condition: The mycelia grown on PDA plates at 28 °C for 3 days were prepared. Five pieces of culture plugs of the strain were inoculated into each 500 mL large-mouth jar containing 150 mL of YMG (glucose 0.4%, malt extract 1.0%, yeast extract 0.4%, pH 5.5) and shaken on a rotatory (150 rpm) at 25 °C for 2 days. Then, the cultures were transferred into eleven 500 mL large-mouth jars containing 150 mL of YMG at the same incubation condition. Finally, 5 mL of the pre-culture broth was transferred into each 500 mL large-mouth jar containing 70 mL of distilled water and 70 g of rice grains, and the incubation was performed in stationary phase at 25 °C for 35 days.

Plant_Material: The strain YM 311647 was obtained from the stem of the apparently healthy Azadirachta indica A. Juss (Meliaceae) and identified as Xylaria sp. (Xylariaceae).
Fermentation_Condition: The prepared fresh mycelium of the strain was inoculated into each of five 500 mL Erlenmeyer flasks containing 150 mL PDB medium (200 g potato and 20 g dextrose in 1 L H2O), and then incubated at 28 °C on a rotary shaker at 180 rpm for 5 days to obtain the seed culture. Fermentation was performed in 500 mL Fernbach flasks ( × 50), each containing 60 g rice, 20 g perlite grain, and 100 mL distilled water. After disinfected at 121 °C for 30 min in autoclave and cooled to room temperature, each flask was inoculated with 10 mL of the seed cultures and incubated at 28 °C for 45 days.

Fermentation was carried out in ﬁfty Erlenmeyer ﬂasks, each containing 100 g of rice (autoclaving at 121 °C for 15 min) with the nutrient solution (0.2% hipo, 0.2% yeast extract, and 0.2% NH4Cl). Each ﬂask was inoculated with 10 mL fungal inocula and incubated at room temperature for 21 days. After 21 days of cultivation, the rice was harvested and used as a sample for further extraction.

Plant_Material: The fungus was isolated from healthy leaves of the plant Origanum majorana according to method of the fungal endophytes’ isolation.
Fermentation_Condition: Agar slants (7 days-old) of M. ruber SRZ112 were flooded by a sterile saline solution then gently scrapping-off spores and finally vortexed for 1 min. To adjust the spore concentration to 106 spore/mL, the collected spores were diluted and counted using a hemocytometer. Production of pigments were achieved using solid-state cultivation as follows; in a 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask 10 g potato peel (substrate) was moistened by 6 mL of the Mineral Salt Broth (pH 6.0) to attain a moisture content of 60%, w/w and autoclaved. After cooling to room temperature, 1 mL of the prepared spore suspension was added to the flask and the contents were thoroughly mixed. The flasks were dark-incubated for 6 days at 25 °C.

Plant_Material: Endophytic fungus Aspergillus creber EN-602 was isolated from fresh tissue of marine red alga Rhodomela confervoides that was collected from the coast of Qingdao, China, in August 2018.
Fermentation_Condition: For chemical investigations, the fresh mycelia of fungus A. creber EN-602 were grown on PDA medium at 28 °C for five days and inoculated on 1 L conical flasks that contained 300 mL of a modified MH2 medium (mannitol 20 g, sucrose 20 g, peptone 5 g, yeast extract 3 g, K2HPO4 0.5 g, MgSO4.7H2O 0.3 g, and 100 g homogenized and broken tissue of fresh marine red alga Rhodomela confervoides in 1000 mL naturally sourced and filtered seawater, which was obtained from the Huiquan Gulf of the Yellow Sea near the campus of IOCAS, which was of pH 6.5–7.0) for 30 days at room temperature. The modified MH2 medium was sterilized at 121 ℃ for 20 min prior to inoculation.

Plant_Material: Chromolaena laevigata (Lam.) R. M. King & H. Rob. (Asteraceae) is a native specimen; it was collected at Ponta Grossa city, Paraná State, Brazil (25° 05′ 16″ S, 50° 05′ 43″ W) in March 2016.
Fermentation_Condition: The CL7 strain was performed on potato dextrose broth (PD) (HiMedia M403) and stationary (PD-S) at pH 6.8. The strain was cultivated in three 1-L Erlenmeyer flasks, each containing 500 mL of medium. A spore solution was prepared at a concentration of 10^7 spores mL−1. Briefly, spores were harvested when the cultures were fully sporulated, which was achieved after 10 days of incubation. The spores were released by flooding the Petri dishes with 5 mL sterile distilled water containing 0.1% (v/v) of tween 80 and the gently rubbing the culture with a sterile L-shaped spreader, a hemocytometer slide was used to count spore concentration. Subsequently, 500 μL of this solution was added to each culture flask. After inoculation, the flasks were stored in a growth greenhouse at 28 °C for 21 days for the stationary cultures and in a shaker culture incubator at 28 °C at 110 rpm for 21 days for the agitated cultures.

Solid fermentation was carried out in 200 Erlenmeyer flasks (1 L) each containing 140 g of rice and 210 mL of distilled water with 5 mmol/L Nicotinamide, 0.1 mmol/L 5-aza-2-deoxycytidine, 0.25 mmol/L CuSO4 ⋅ 5H2O, 0.5 g/L MgSO4 and 0.5 g/L NaCl were sterilized at autoclave, and then, 10 mL of seed culture was added into each flask. All flasks were incubated at 28 °C for 30 days.
Assay_Description: PC12 cell injury induced by glutamate

A large-scale fermentation was incubated statically at 25 °C under a normal day/night cycle for 30 days using a rice medium composed of 120 g of rice, 3 g of sea salt, 1.5 g bacterial peptone, 150 mL of distilled H2O in the 1 L flask ( × 42).

A large-scale fermentation was incubated statically at 25 °C under a normal day/night cycle for 30 days using a rice medium composed of 120 g of rice, 3 g of sea salt, 1.5 g bacterial peptone, 150 mL of distilled H2O in the 1 L flask ( × 42).

A large-scale fermentation was incubated statically at 25 °C under a normal day/night cycle for 30 days using a rice medium composed of 120 g of rice, 3 g of sea salt, 1.5 g bacterial peptone, 150 mL of distilled H2O in the 1 L flask ( × 42).

Plant_Material: An endophytic isolate (B4) was isolated from fresh stems of healthy Artemisia annua plants (collected in July 2008 in Zijin Mount of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, China).
Fermentation_Condition: P. oxalicum B4 was inoculated on PDA plates for 5 days at 28 °C. Then mycelial plug (5 mm diameter) was transferred to a 150-mL Erlenmeyer flask containing 50 mL of the minimal media (30 g/L sucrose, 5 g/L peptone, 3 g/L NaCl, 3 g/L NaH2PO4, 3 g/L NaNO3, 5 g/L MgSO4.3H2O, 4.15 g/L KCl, 1 g/L FeSO4.7H2O and 1 g/L MnSO4, pH6.0) and cultured on a rotary shaker (Hualida HZ-9311 K, Taicang, China) at 150 rpm and 28 °C for 48 h. The AA/acetone solution (the concentration of mother liquor was 200 mg/mL) was added into the cultures (3.50 mg per 50.00 mL medium in each Erlenmeyer flask). The biotransformation was carried out in shake-flask cultures (one batch of 21 flasks) for a further 13 days.

Then mycelial plug (5 mm diameter) was transferred to a 150-mL Erlenmeyer flask containing 50 mL of the minimal media (30 g/L sucrose, 5 g/L peptone, 3 g/L NaCl, 3 g/L NaH2PO4, 3 g/L NaNO3, 5 g/L MgSO4.3H2O, 4.15 g/L KCl, 1 g/L FeSO4.7H2O and 1 g/L MnSO4, pH6.0) and cultured on a rotary shaker (Hualida HZ-9311 K, Taicang, China) at 150 rpm and 28 °C for 48 h. The AA/acetone solution (the concentration of mother liquor was 200 mg/mL) was added into the cultures (3.50 mg per 50.00 mL medium in each Erlenmeyer flask). The biotransformation was carried out in shake-flask cultures (one batch of 21 flasks) for a further 13 days.

The seed was cultured at 30 °C, 250 rpm for another 4 days and then every 25 mL of the seed medium was transferred into 1L Erlenmeyer flask, which contained 250 mL of YMG. The production medium (20 L) was cultured at 30 °C, 200 rpm for 14 days.

Fermentation_Condition: The strain has been maintained on slant tubes of potato dextrose agars (PDA) medium (potato 200 g, glucose 20 g, distilled water 1 L, agar 8 g, pH 6.0, the media was autoclaved at 115 °C for 30 min) at 4 °C in the State Key Laboratory of Phytochemistry and Plant Resources in West China. Plant_Material: The fungus P. acaciicola was isolated from the healthy roots of a mangrove tree, Bruguiera gymnorrhiza, collected in November 2012 at The Mangrove Forest Learning and Development Center 2, Samut Sakhon province, Thailand.
Fermentation_Condition: The fungus P. acaciicola was cultured on Potato Dextrose Agar (PDA) (HiMedia Laboratories, Mumbai, India) containing 10% of seawater (collected from Bang Saen Beach, Chonburi Province) for 1 week. After incubation for 21 days, broth (total volume of 500 mL) and fungal mycelia were separated by filtration using filter paper (Whatman, Grade 1).

Plant_Material: Pestalotiopsis sp. was isolated from a surface sterilised piece of stem (∼2 mm × 10 mm) from the plant Melaleuca quinquenervia collected from Toohey Forest, Queensland, Australia during February of 2003.
Fermentation_Condition: The fungal isolate (BRIP 39872) was initially grown on potato dextrose agar, until a prominent growth of mycelia was achieved. The mycelia covered agar was then cut into ∼1 cm3 portions, and transferred to six conical flasks (500 mL) each containing sterilised damp white rice (50 g rice plus 100 mL H2O). The fermentation was allowed to proceed under static conditions at 25 °C for 28 days after which time the rice and mycelia were extracted with EtOAc (3 × 150 mL).

The mycelia covered agar was then cut into ∼1 cm3 portions, and transferred to six conical flasks (500 mL) each containing sterilised damp white rice (50 g rice plus 100 mL H2O). The fermentation was allowed to proceed under static conditions at 25 °C for 28 days after which time the rice and mycelia were extracted with EtOAc (3 × 150 mL).

Plant_Material: The strains discussed in this paper were isolated from white pine branches collected from healthy trees between 70 and 100 years old in stands (45°25′17.282″N 66°30′10.135″W) near St. George, New Brunswick.
Fermentation_Condition: For inoculation, a slant of each strain was macerated in sterile ddH2O under aseptic conditions. The resulting suspension was used to inoculate (5%, v:v) fifteen 250 mL Erlenmeyer flasks each containing 50 mL of 2% malt extract (Difco) medium. The starter cultures were allowed to grow for two weeks, macerated and individually transferred to corresponding Glaxo bottles containing 1 L of the same medium. These were incubated for eight weeks at 25 °C.

Plant_Material: The isolation of endophytic fungi from healthy wild ginger tissues.
Fermentation_Condition: Cultivation broth consisted of Potato Dextrose Broth (PDB), Difco (Potato Starch 4, Dextrose 20 g/L), and used directly at pH 5.2. The Potato Dextrose Agar (PDA) consisted of PDB supplemented with agar (Difco) at a final concentration of 20%. Prior to the cultivation step, Petri dishes were inoculated with a frozen sample for 5 days. Four milliliters of medium was then spread on the agar layer. The spores-mycelium mixture was used to inoculate shake-flasks containing PDB medium. The strain was then allowed to grow in a rotary shaker (3 × 1L) at 27 °C and 200 rpm for 5 days.

The Potato Dextrose Agar (PDA) consisted of PDB supplemented with agar (Difco) at a final concentration of 20%. Prior to the cultivation step, Petri dishes were inoculated with a frozen sample for 5 days. Four milliliters of medium was then spread on the agar layer. The spores-mycelium mixture was used to inoculate shake-flasks containing PDB medium. The strain was then allowed to grow in a rotary shaker (3 × 1L) at 27 °C and 200 rpm for 5 days.

Plant_Material: The herb Bidens pilosa (Asteraceae) has been collected at the museum of agriculture in Cairo, Egypt. To obtain the endophyte from within the stem parts of the plant.
Fermentation_Condition: Both the chemical and biological analyses showed that the antimicrobial activity of the fungal extract and the production of secondary metabolites were highest using a stationary culture (21 days) at 23 °C of M25, a cornsteep medium composed of sucrose (20 g l−1), soy bean starch (10 g l−1), cornsteep (10 g l−1) completed with distilled water to 1 l (pH 6.5). The fungus was grown on potato dextrose agar (PDA) at 23 °C for 14 days and the mycelium of each plate was cut into 12 pieces each of which was used as an inoculum in a 1 l Erlenmeyer flask, containing 250 ml of M25. Incubation was carried out for 21 days (23 °C) under static conditions.

Plant_Material: The Podospora sp. was isolated from the Kenyan medicinal plant Laggera alata (Asteraceae) collected from the edges of the Mau forest in the Rift Valley Province.
Fermentation_Condition: The endophytic Podospora sp. was cultivated in 20 of 1-L Erlenmeyer flasks each containing 250 mL M2-medium (5 g malt extract, 2 g yeast extract and 2 g glucose per litre tap water, adjusted to pH 7 8 and autoclaved at 129 °C for 20 min). The flasks were inoculated with approximately 1 × 1 cm pieces of a 4-day-old culture of the fungus on M2 agar kept at 28 °C and sealed with pieces of cloth to permit aerobic growth. After incubation for 4 days on a linear shaker at 28 °C and 95 rpm, the culture broth (5 L) was used to inoculate a Braun Biostat U fermentor (Braun, Melsungen, Germany) containing 20 L of M2 medium. The fermentation was done at the following conditions: stirring rate 200 rpm, 28 °C, pH regulation 6.5 ± 1.5, aeration 1.5 m3/h.

Plant_Material: The fungal strain Epicoccum nigrum (W-2) was isolated from the stem tuber of Pinellia ternate (thunb.) Berit. which were collected from the Gansu Province, China, in September 2016.

Three pieces (0.3 × 0.3 × 0.3 cm3 ) of agar plugs were transferred aseptically into a 500 mL Erlenmeyer flask containing 200 mL of potato dextrose liquid medium, incubated on a rotary shaker at 28 °C and 180 rpm for 4 days to prepare seed culture. Solid fermentation was carried out in 5 Erlenmeyer flasks (2.5L) each containing 320 g of sterilized rice and 70 mL of seed culture at 28 °C for 45 days.

Plant_Material: Strain Kitasatospora sp. CPCC 204717 was isolated from the leaf of Huperzia serrata collected in Nanping, Fujian province , China.

One piece of mycelial agar plug (about 1 cm2 ) was inoculated into 500 mL Fernbach flasks containing 100 mL of the TCG medium (composed of 3 g of tryptone, 5 g of casitone, and 4 g of glucose in 1 L of water, pH 7.2) at 28 °C for 3 days. An aliquot (10 mL) of the resulting cultures was used to inoculate into 50 replicate 500 mL Fernbach flasks each containing 100 mL of the rice medium (100 g of rice, 0.3 g of peptone in 100 mLwater). After growing at 28 °C for 30 days.

Plant_Material: The strain A761 was isolated from the plant Morinda of icinalis, which was collected from Gaoyao city of Guangdong province in January 2015.
Fermentation_Condition: Cytospora rhizophorae A761 was cultured in potato dextrose broth (potato 20%, glucose 2%, K2HPO4 0.3%, MgSO4•7H2O 0.15%, vitamin B 10 mg/L). The fungus C. rhizophorae A761 was maintained on potato dextrose agar (PDA) medium at 28 °C for 5 days, and then three pieces (0.5 × 0.5 cm2) of mycelial agar plugs were inoculated into 20 × 500 mL Erlenmeyer flasks, each containing 250 mL potato dextrose broth. After 4 days of incubation at 28 °C on a rotary shaker at 120 r/m, 25 mL seed cultures was aseptically transferred into the 1000 mL flask (a total of 150 flasks), which was contained 500 mL of potato dextrose broth. The liquid cultivation that followed was kept for 7 days at 28 °C and 120 r/m on a rotary shaker.

Plant_Material: The fungal strain Phomopsis sp. TJ507A was isolated from the fresh branches of the medicinally important plant Phyllanthus glaucus, which was collected at Lushan Mountain of Jiangxi Province, People’s Republic of China, in August 2014.

After 35 days, the fermented rice substrate was extracted five times with EtOAc at room temperature.

Plant_Material: The fungus P. sumatrense MA-92 was isolated from the rhizosphere of the marine mangrove plant Lumnitzera racemosa collected at WenChang in Hainan Island, P. R. China, in July 2010.
Fermentation_Condition: The fresh mycelium was inoculated into 1 L flask preloaded with 400 mL of Czapek medium (consisting of 14 g glucose, 9.6 g mannitol, 1.4 g NaNO3, 0.6 g KH2PO4, 0.3 g MgSO4, 1.2 g sodium glutamate, 0.6 g sodium tartrate, 6 g sea salt) followed by a four-day culture at 200 rpm/min and 28 o C. The whole liquid (10 × 400 mL) collected from the flask was inoculated onto a 50-L seed tank containing 38 L of sterilized Czapek medium (antifoam 0.5‰, aeration rate 2000NL/h, 150 rpm/min) After a subsequent fermentation at 28 o C for 24 h, the afforded liquid was transferred as seed into a 500 L fermentor preloaded with 300 L of sterilized Czapek medium prior to cultivation at 28 o C for 4 days (antifoam 0.5‰, aeration rate 6000NL/h, 150 rpm/min).

Plant_Material: The strain A761 was isolated from the plant Morinda of icinalis, which was collected from Gaoyao city of Guangdong province in January 2015.
Fermentation_Condition: Cytospora rhizophorae A761 was cultured in potato dextrose broth (potato 20%, glucose 2%, K2HPO4 0.3%, MgSO4•7H2O 0.15%, vitamin B 10 mg/L). The fungus C. rhizophorae A761 was maintained on potato dextrose agar (PDA) medium at 28 °C for 5 days, and then three pieces (0.5 × 0.5 cm2) of mycelial agar plugs were inoculated into 20 × 500 mL Erlenmeyer flasks, each containing 250 mL potato dextrose broth. After 4 days of incubation at 28 °C on a rotary shaker at 120 r/m, 25 mL seed cultures were aseptically transferred into each of a total of 100 flasks (1000 mL) containing 500 mL of potato dextrose broth. The liquid cultivation that followed was kept for 7 days at 28 °C and 120 r/m on a rotary shaker.

Plant_Material: Pestalotiopsis sp. was isolated from a surface sterilised piece of stem (∼ 2 mm × 10 mm) from the plant Melaleuca quinquenervia collected from Toohey Forest, Queensland, Australia during February of 2003.
Fermentation_Condition: The fungal isolate (BRIP 39872) was initially grown on potato dextrose agar, until a prominent growth of mycelia was achieved. The mycelia covered agar was then cut into ∼1 cm3 portions, and then transferred to three conical flasks (500 mL) each containing sterilised damp white rice (50 g rice plus 100 mL H2O). The fermentation was allowed to proceed under static conditions at 25 °C for 28 days after which time the rice and mycelia were extracted with EtOAc (3 × 150 mL).

Plant_Material: Panax ginseng was collected from Ji-an City (Jilin, China) and had been grown for 30 years in the forest.
Fermentation_Condition: The endophytic bacteria were grown in PDA broth at 30°C until its absorbance at 600 nm reached 1.0. Then, it was mixed with the same volume of ginsenoside Rb1 (1 mg ml−1) and incubated at 30°C in shaking incubator. During the reaction period, the reaction mixture was collected every 12 h, extracted with water saturated n-butanol and then analysed by both TLC and HPLC methods.

Plant_Material: Living, fresh, and apparently healthy individuals of the tropical grass Paspalum conjugatum (Poaceae; buffalo grass, carabao grass, or sour paspalum) were collected in Colon, Panama.
Fermentation_Condition: The fungus F2611 was pre-cultured in 400 ml malt extract broth (MEB, Sigma-Aldrich) for 10 days to generate a large mycelial mass. A thin layer of liquid pre-culture (5–7 ml) was used to inoculate the surface of (MEA) medium in 145 mm Petri dishes. The liquid evaporated after 4–6 days and thus saturated the agar surface with fungal biomass. F2611 was cultured for 24 days in 150 MEA petri dishes (10 l MEA) with constant light and at room temperature (25–30°C).

Plant_Material: Healthy Schefflera leucantha leaves were collected from Chiang Rai province, northern Thailand (19° 56′ 10.118″ N, 99° 51′ 9.801″ E) in July 2018 (weather conditions: 27 °C with 80–100% humidity).
Fermentation_Condition: PDA was used as the medium. In this experiment, 2 Petri bottom plates (92 mm × 16 mm) were used. The first plate was inoculated with either a mycelial plug (5 mm diameter) of 7-day old Fusarium oxysporum or Fusarium proliferatum culture. The second plate hosted a 7-day old culture of either MFLUCC19-0090 or MFLUCC19-0091. Two plates were placed, face-to-face, against each other and carefully wrapped with Parafilm to prevent vapors from leaking.

Plant_Material: Chaetomium sp. g1 as a plant endophyte was isolated from the fresh stem inner tissue of the Isodon eriocalyx var. laxiflora collected from Kunming Botanical Garden, Kunming, People’s Republic of China, in December 2012.
Fermentation_Condition: Fermentation was carried out in 550 Fernbach flasks (500 mL), each containing 100 g of rice. Spore inoculum was prepared in sterile, distilled H2O to give a final spore/cell suspension of 1 × 106/mL. Distilled H2O (120 mL) was added to each flask, and the contents were soaked overnight before autoclaving at 15 psi for 30 min. After cooling to room temperature, each flask was inoculated with 5.0 mL of the spore inoculum and incubated at indoor temperature for 42 days.

Spore inoculum was prepared in sterile, distilled H2O to give a final spore/cell suspension of 1 × 106/mL. Distilled H2O (120 mL) was added to each flask, and the contents were soaked overnight before autoclaving at 15 psi for 30 min. After cooling to room temperature, each flask was inoculated with 5.0 mL of the spore inoculum and incubated at indoor temperature for 42 days.

Plant_Material: The fungus used in this study was an endophytic strain of E. nigrum, YEF2 (IRAN 2950C), which was isolated from the bud of Taxus baccata grown in Iran.
Fermentation_Condition: The highest total yield of paclitaxel in co-culture established on 13th day (404.5 µg L−1) was produced by using 3.2% (v/v) E. nigrum mycelium suspension (EMS).Four agar plugs (5 mm diameter) containing the mycelia from 10-day-old culture of strain YEF2 grown on potato dextrose agar (PDA) medium at 25 °C were cultured in 250-mL Erlenmeyer flasks containing 100 mL PDB medium and incubated on the shaker at 110 rpm at 25 °C for 12 days. Callus of hazel (C. avellana ecotype Gerd Ashkorat) was obtained from seed cotyledons on Murashige and Skoog (MS) medium supplemented with 0.2 mg L−1 BAP and 2 mg L−1 2,4-D and solidified with 8 g L−1 agar agar.

Plant_Material: Healthy samples including the bark pieces, stem, bud and leaves were collected from Taxus baccata grown at the botanical garden of College of Agriculture and Natural Resources (36°40'01″N, 51°10'18″ E at an altitude of 1321 m), University of Tehran, located in Karaj, Alborz Province of Iran, in July and September 2014.
Fermentation_Condition: The experiment was carried out with three replications. Each replication consisted of 100 ml flask containing 30 ml MS medium supplemented with 0.2 mg/l BAP, 2 mg/l GA3 and 2 mg/l 2,4-D. The inoculum was prepared from 7-day-old cultures of strain YEF2 grown on PDA medium at 25 °C. Two mycelial agar plugs (5 mm diameter) per replication were cut from the margin of the growing colony using a sterilized cork borer. Cultures were maintained at 25 °C in darkness on gyratory shakers at 110 rpm. (Control (without elicitor))

Plant_Material: The Gram-positive filamentous aerobic bacterium Streptomyces sp. AC35 was isolated from the rhizosphere of higher tree Taxus baccata, from the Bratislava region, Slovakia.
Fermentation_Condition: Batch cultivation was carried out in 3.0 l-Brunswick BioFlo R 115 fermenters (Eppendorf, Hamburg, Germany) with 1.8 l of production media. Conditions within the laboratory fermenters were as follows: 10 % v/v inoculum (prepared as outlined above), dissolved oxygen (DO) maintained at 20 % with agitation cascade 50–1000 rpm, constant temperature at 28 °C. The effects of different pH conditions on extract production were studied. In fermenter No. 1 (BC1), pH 7.0 was maintained with 1 M NaOH solution, while in fermenter No. 2 (BC2), pH was set at 7.0 at the initial hour of fermentation but was not maintained throughout the process. 220 μl of Delamex (Fermas, Slovakia) was added per 1 l of medium as an antifoam agent. Sterile medium with an identical composition to the production medium, but without microorganisms, was incubated under the same conditions as the substrate control.

Plant_Material: Phomopsis sp. Hant25 from a Thai medicinal plant, Hydnocarpus anthelminthicus.
Fermentation_Condition: A 50-ml volume of culture broth was distributed in 250-ml Erlenmeyer flasks (Pyrex 4980), closed with cotton wool plugs, covered with aluminum foil and sterilized by autoclaving. In the experiments with solid supports, the following materials were used: cellulose paper (Whatman chromatography paper, No. 1 Chr). The sheets were cut into 7-cm diameter circular discs, cleaned by autoclaving in water and dried at 60°C. A disc made of one layer, or four layers in the case of absorbent cotton gauze, was placed in each culture flask and autoclaved together with the medium. Throughout this study, fermentation was started by inoculating the culture flask with 2 agar plugs containing mycelia punched from agar plates as described above. Incubation was at 25°C under static conditions, with continuous shaking at 120 rpm or with a combination of stasis followed by shaking at 120 rpm.

Plant_Material: The fungus was isolated from fresh seeds of Raphia teadigera collected in January 2015 in Haut Plateaux region, Cameroon.
Fermentation_Condition: Ten Erlenmeyer flasks (1 L each, two flasks for axenic Bacillus subtilis 168 trpC2, two for axenic Bionectria sp. and six for co-culture) containing 60 mL of distilled water and 50 g of commercially available milk rice (Milch-Reis, ORYZA) were autoclaved before inoculation. An overnight culture of B. subtilis grown in lysogeny broth (LB) was used to inoculate prewarmed LB medium (1:20), which was then incubated at 37 °C with shaking at 200 rpm to mid exponential growth phase (optical density at 600 nm of 0.2–0.4). To the rice medium was added 10 mL of the bacterial culture followed by incubation at 37 °C. After four days, four pieces (1 cm × 1 cm) of Bionectria sp. grown on malt agar were added to the flasks that had been preincubated with B. subtilis. Fungal and bacterial controls were grown axenically on solid rice medium. Co-cultures and axenic cultures of Bionectria sp. and B. subtilis were kept at 21 °C under static conditions until they reached their stationary phase of growth (3 weeks for controls of Bionectria sp. and B. subtilis, 4 weeks for co-cultures).

Plant_Material: The endophytic fungus Fusarium sp. HP-2 was isolated from Chinese agarwood “Qi-Nan”, collected in Ledong County, Hainan Province, PR China in 2011.
Fermentation_Condition: The endophytic fungus Fusarium sp. HP-2 was inoculated and cultured on a PDA agar for 7 days. A piece of mycelial agar plugs (0.5 cm × 0.5 cm) were inoculated into 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask containing potato dextrose broth (PDB) (80 mL). The culture was shaked at 120 rpm at room temperature for three days. Production medium of solid rice in 1000 mL Erlenmeyer flasks was inoculated with 10 mL seed solution for each one. Erlenmeyer flasks were incubated at room temperature under static conditions for 45 days, and cultures from 200 Erlenmeyer flasks were harvested for the isolation of substances.

Plant_Material: The strain numbered as J13-1-6J was isolated from the Houttuynia cordata Thunb. collected from Guangxi Medicinal Botanical Garden, Guangxi Province, People's Republic of China.
Fermentation_Condition: The fungus was cultured on slants of potato dextrose agar at 25 °C for 5 days. Agar plugs were used to inoculate four Erlenmeyer flasks (250 mL), each containing 100 mL of potato dextrose broth. The four flasks of the inoculated media were incubated at 25 °C on a rotary shaker at 200 rpm for 5 days to prepare the seed culture. Fermentation was carried out in 22 Erlenmeyer flasks (500 mL), each containing 70 g of rice. Distilled H2O (110 mL) was added to each flask, and then autoclaving at 120 °C for 30 min. After cooling to room temperature, each flask was inoculated with 5.0 mL of the spore inoculum and incubated at room temperature for 45 days.

Three flasks of the inoculated medium were incubated at 25 °C on a rotary shaker at 170 rpm for 5 days to prepare the seed culture. Distilled H2O (120 mL) was added to each flask, and the contents were soaked overnight before being autoclaved at 15 psi for 30 min. After cooling to room temperature, each flask was inoculated with 5.0 mL of the spore inoculum and incubated at 25 °C for 40 days.

Plant_Material: The title strain was isolated from the branches of Camellia sinensis, collected from the suburb of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, People's Republic of China, in October 2012.
Fermentation_Condition: The fungal strain was cultivated on PDA medium at 28 °C until sufficient growth was observed (about 5 days). Then plugs of agar supporting mycelia growth were cut into small pieces and transferred aseptically into a 1000 ml Erlenmeyer flask containing 300 ml potato dextrose broth, and incubated on a rotary shaker at 180 rpm for 7 days to prepare the seed culture. Fermentation was carried out in ten 500 ml Erlenmeyer flasks, each containing 80 g of rice and soaked with 120 ml distilled water overnight before autoclaving. Each flask was inoculated with 10 ml seed liquid, and cultivated under stationary conditions at 28 °C for 30 days.

Plant_Material: The culture of Exserohilum sp. was isolated from the leaves of A. truncatum Bunge, collected from Dongling Mountain, Beijing, People's Republic of China, in August, 2007.
Fermentation_Condition: The fungal strain was cultured on slants of potato dextrose agar (PDA) at 25 °C for 10 days. Agar plugs were cut into small pieces (about 0.5 × 0.5 × 0.5 cm3) under aseptic conditions, and 15 pieces were used to inoculate three Erlenmeyer flasks (250 mL), each containing 50 mL of media (0.4% glucose, 1% malt extract, and 0.4% yeast extract; the final pH of the media was adjusted to 6.5 and sterilized by autoclave). Three flasks of the inoculated media were incubated at 25 °C on a rotary shaker at 170 rpm for five days to prepare the seed culture. Fermentation was carried out in 12 Fernbach flasks (500 mL), each containing 80 g of rice. Distilled H2O (120 mL) was added to each flask, and the contents were soaked overnight before autoclaving at 15 psi for 30 min. After cooling to room temperature, each flask was inoculated with 5.0 mL of the spore inoculum and incubated at 25 °C for 40 days.

Agar plugs were cut into small pieces (about 0.5 × 0.5 × 0.5 cm3) under aseptic conditions, and 15 pieces were used to inoculate three Erlenmeyer flasks (250 mL), each containing 50 mL of media (0.4% glucose, 1% malt extract, and 0.4% yeast extract; the final pH of the media was adjusted to 6.5 and sterilized by autoclave). Three flasks of the inoculated media were incubated at 25 °C on a rotary shaker at 170 rpm for five days to prepare the seed culture. Fermentation was carried out in 12 Fernbach flasks (500 mL), each containing 80 g of rice. Distilled H2O (120 mL) was added to each flask, and the contents were soaked overnight before autoclaving at 15 psi for 30 min. After cooling to room temperature, each flask was inoculated with 5.0 mL of the spore inoculum and incubated at 25 °C for 40 days.

Plant_Material: The culture of P. fici was isolated from the branches of Camellia sinensis (Theaceae) in a suburb of Hangzhou, People's Republic of China, in April, 2005.
Fermentation_Condition: The fungal strain was cultured on slants of potato dextrose agar (PDA) at 25 °C for 10 days. Agar plugs were cut into small pieces (about 0.5 × 0.5 × 0.5 cm3) under aseptic conditions and 15 pieces were used to inoculate three Erlenmeyer flasks (250 mL), each containing 50 mL of media (0.4% glucose, 1% malt extract, and 0.4% yeast extract); the final pH of the media was adjusted to 6.5 and sterilized by autoclave. Three flasks of the inoculated media were incubated at 25 °C on a rotary shaker at 170 rpm for five days to prepare the seed culture. Spore inoculum was prepared by suspension in sterile, distilled H2O to give a final spore/cell suspension of 1 × 106/mL. Fermentation was carried out in 12 Fernbach flasks (500 mL), each containing 80 g of rice. Distilled H2O (120 mL) was added to each flask, and the contents were soaked overnight before autoclaving at 15 psi for 30 min. After cooling to room temperature, each flask was inoculated with 5.0 mL of the spore inoculum and incubated at 25 °C for 40 days.

Agar plugs were inoculated in 500-mL Erlenmeyer flask containing 120 mL of media (0.4% glucose, 1% malt extract, and 0.4% yeast extract), and the final pH of the media was adjusted to 6.5 before sterilization, and incubated at 25 °C on a rotary shaker at 180 rpm for 7 days. Large scale fermentation was carried out in 27 bottles of 500-mL Fernbach flasks each containing 150 mL of the Czapek's medium (sucrose 3%, NaNO3 0.3%, KH2PO4 0.1%, MgSO4.7H2O 0.05%, KCl 0.05%, FeSO4 0.001%). Each flask was inoculated with a culture medium of 5.0 mL and incubated at 25 °C for 14 days on a rotary shaker at 180 rpm.

Plant_Material: The culture of T. gamsii was isolated from traditional Chinese medicinal plant Panax notoginseng (BurK.) F.H.Chen.
Fermentation_Condition: The fungal strain was cultured on slants of potato dextrose agar (PDA) at 25 °C for 10 days. The agar plugs were used to inoculate 250 mL Erlenmeyer flasks, each containing 40 mL of media (0.4% glucose, 1% malt extract, and 0.4% yeast extract), and the final pH of the media was adjusted to 6.5 before sterilization. Flask cultures were incubated at 25 °C on a rotary shaker at 170 rpm for five days. Fermentation was carried out in Fernbach flasks (500 mL) each containing 80 g of rice. Spore inoculum was prepared by suspension in sterile, distilled H2O to give a final spore/cell suspension of 1 × 106/mL. Distilled H2O (100 mL) was added to each flask, and the contents were soaked overnight before autoclaving at 15 lb/in− 2 for 30 min. After cooling to room temperature, each flask was inoculated with 5.0 mL of the spore inoculum and incubated at 25 °C for 40 days.

Agar plugs were inoculated in 500 mL Erlenmeyer flask containing 120 mL of media (0.4% glucose, 1% malt extract, and 0.4% yeast extract). The final pH of the media was adjusted to 6.5 before sterilization. The agar pugs in media were then incubated at 25 °C on a rotary shaker at 170 rpm for one week. Large scale fermentation was carried out in twenty 500 mL Fernbach flasks each containing 80 g of rice and 120 mL of distilled H2O. Each flask was inoculated with 5.0 mL of the culture medium and incubated at 25 °C for 40 days.

Plant_Material: The SKJM1101 strain was isolated from medicinally important plant Piper nigrum collected from Coonoor, Nilgiri district of Tamil Nadu, India.
Fermentation_Condition: The fungal strain SKJM1101 was grown on MID medium (supplemented with 1 gm soytone L−1) agar plates at 25°C for 7 days. After 3 weeks, the entire culture was harvested by passing through two layers of cheese cloth separating mycelia mat and culture filtrate.

Plant_Material: Healthy leaves and small branches of G. biloba were collected from plants from April to September 2009 located in Taixing and Nanjing in Jiangsu Province and Chengdu in Sichuan Province, P.R. China.
Fermentation_Condition: Endophytic fungal isolates were grown on PDA medium (potato 200 g, dextrose 20 g, agar 20 g, H2O 1000 mL) at 25 °C for the appropriate number of days. Eight pieces (5 mm diameter) of mycelial agar plugs removed from the edge of young cultures of endophytic fungi were each inoculated into 250-mL Erlenmeyer flasks with 100 mL PD broth medium, followed by shaking (150 rpm) continuously for 12 days at 25 ± 1 °C. The broth culture was filtered to separate the culture broth and mycelia. The culture broth was refiltered with a 0.22-µm bacterial filter to obtain the sterile fermentation broth, which was subsequently kept at 4 °C.

Plant_Material: Leaves from Trixis vauthieri DC (Asteraceae) were collected at the ‘RPPN Santuário do Caraça’ natural preserve, located in the municipality of Catas Altas, state of Minas Gerais, Brazil.
Fermentation_Condition: Briefly, the fungus was cultivated in solid MEC (2% malt extract, 0.1% peptone, 1.5% glucose) medium and then inoculated into 40 flasks containing 25 mL of liquid MEC medium. The flasks were incubated in a shaker (150 r.p.m.) for 5 days at 28 °C. The contents of each flask were transferred to fourty 250-mL Erlenmeyer flasks, each containing 100 mL of MEC medium, and incubated in the shaker for 9 days at 28 °C.

Each flask contained 3 L malt extract broth culture medium (malt extract 2 %, glucose 2 %, and bacterial peptone 0.1 %). Altogether, a total of 15 L was fermented statically at room temperature in the dark for 45 days.

Plant_Material: The fungus QJF-22 was obtained from a healthy twig of the marine mangrove Kandelia candel, which was gathered in August 2016 from Haikou East Harbor National Nature Reserve in Hainan Province, China.
Fermentation_Condition: The fungus was activated and cultured on potato dextrose broth (PDB) 4×1 L-Erlenmeyer flasks at 28 °C for a week in shaker to obtain spore inoculum. The routine-scale fermentation was performed in 60×1 L-Erlenmeyer flasks, each containing 50 gram rice and 50 milliliter of 0.3 % saline. The Erlenmeyer flask containing the culture medium was autoclaved at 121 °C for 30 min. After cooling to room temperature, 20 mL of inoculum were inoculated in each bottle and incubated at room temperature for 30 days.
Assay_Description: Nitric oxide (NO) production in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced RAW 264.7 macrophages

After cooling to room temperature, 20 mL of inoculum were inoculated in each bottle and incubated at room temperature for 30 days.

Plant_Material: Healthy Gentiana rigescens plants (specimen No. 2010040) were collected from Zhenxiong city, Yunnan Province.
Fermentation_Condition: Endophytic fungi first underwent culture on PDA in petri dishes. Then, 5 mm dimeter agar plate cultures were added to Erlenmeyer flasks (5) containing sterilized PDB for fermentation at 28 °C and 180 rpm in a ZHWY-211 incubator (Zhicheng Analytical Instrument Manufacturing, China). A biotransformation assay, alongside culture and substrate controls were run to screen microorganisms for evaluating their biotransformation activities for gentiopicroside and swertiamarin. Fungi in 50 mL (150 mL flasks) of PDB were incubated at 28 °C and 180 rpm for 3 days. Then, gentiopicroside and swertiamarin, respectively, were added to the fermentation broth under sterile conditions. The incubation proceeded for 6 additional days. Three triplicate assays were performed.

Plant_Material: Strain SCSIO 41022 was isolated from the inside of the leaves of mangrove plant Kandelia candel, collected from Daya Bay in Shenzhen city, Guangdong Province, China, in March 2012.

Plant_Material: Pestalotiopsis foedan was isolated from the branches of Bruguiera sexangula in Hainan, P. R. China, in April 2008.
Fermentation_Condition: The fungal strain was cultured on slants of potato dextrose agar (PDA) at 30 °C for 5 d, and then inoculated into 500 ml Erlenmeyer flasks containing 100 ml of PDB. After 7 d of incubation at 30 °C on rotary shakers at 160 rpm, 20 ml of culture liquid was transferred as inoculum into 1000 ml Erlenmeyer flasks containing 200 ml of PDB. Fermentation was carried out at 30 °C on rotary shakers at 150 rpm for 22 d.

Plant_Material: Endophytic actinobacteria were screened from the leaves and roots of healthy Lychnophora ericoides Mart., Asteraceae. The plants were harvested in Furnas (20°15′318″S; 46°15′318″W), in the State of Minas Gerais, Brazil.
Fermentation_Condition: Each stored strain was reactivated in ISP2 liquid medium and plated on ISP2 agar. Plates were incubated for 7 days at 30 °C. Two 5 mm diameter plugs of actinobacteria agar culture were transferred to 10 ml of ISP2 liquid medium contained in Falcon tubes and incubated on a rotary shaker at 30 °C and 120 rpm for 48 h (preculture). The preculture was transferred to a 500-ml Erlenmeyer flask containing solid rice medium (90 g of rice and 90 ml of distilled water). The fermentation culture was incubated at 30 °C for 21 days.

Two 5 mm diameter plugs of actinobacteria agar culture were transferred to 10 ml of ISP2 liquid medium contained in Falcon tubes and incubated on a rotary shaker at 30 °C and 120 rpm for 48 h (preculture). The preculture was transferred to a 500-ml Erlenmeyer flask containing solid rice medium (90 g of rice and 90 ml of distilled water). The fermentation culture was incubated at 30 °C for 21 days.

Fermentation_Condition: The fungus was cultured in 500 mL Erlenmeyer flasks, each containing 40 g rice and 60 mL distilled water, a total of 200 flasks. After incubation for 45 days at 28 °C, the ferments were extracted with methanol thoroughly by ultrasonic, and evaporated under vacuum to afford 10 L aqueous solution.

Plant_Material: The strain YXf3 was isolated by one of the authors (Z.K.G.) from a healthy leaf of Ginkgo biloba collected in the campus of Nanjing University (Nanjing, P. R. China), in October 2008.
Fermentation_Condition: The endophyte fungus was identified as Aspergillus sp. and preserved on PDA medium slants at 4 °C. The fungus was subcultured in 1000 mL Erlenmeyer flasks with 300 mL ME liquid media (consisting of 20 g/L malt extract, 20 g/L sucrose, 1 g/L peptone, and deionized water) on a rotary shaker (140 rpm) at 28 °C for 5 days. Fermentation was then carried out on a platform at 28 °C for 32 days in 250 mL flasks on solid medium containing bran (7.5 g), millet (7.5 g), yeast extract (5 g), sodium glutamate (0.1 g), sodium tartrate (0.1 g), ferric sulfite (0.01 g), and 10 mL H2O per flask.

IFB-YXS into 1000 ml flasks containing 400 ml of ME broth. After 4 days of the incubation at 28 °C on rotary shaker at 140 rpm, 15–20 ml of culture liquid was transferred as the seed into 250 ml flasks each containing 7.5 g millet, 0.5 g yeast extract, 0.1 g tartrate sodium, 0.1 g glutamine sodium, 0.01 g iron vitriol land five drops of pure corn oil. 15 ml of water was added before the fermentation. In the 35-day solid medium cultivation, culture temperature was set at 28 °C and relative humidity in the incubation room at 60–70% with initial water content of the medium at approximately 67%.

IFB-YXS into 1000 ml flasks containing 400 ml of ME broth. After 4 days of the incubation at 28 °C on rotary shaker at 140 rpm, 15–20 ml of culture liquid was transferred as the seed into 250 ml flasks each containing 7.5 g millet, 0.5 g yeast extract, 0.1 g tartrate sodium, 0.1 g glutamine sodium, 0.01 g iron vitriol land five drops of pure corn oil. 15 ml of water was added before the fermentation. In the 35-day solid medium cultivation, culture temperature was set at 28 °C and relative humidity in the incubation room at 60–70% with initial water content of the medium at approximately 67%.

Plant_Material: CR252M was obtained as an endophytic isolate from the leaves of Disterigma humboldtii, collected in Braulio Carrilo National Park (collection permit R-012-2005-OT-CONAGEBIO) in January, 2006.
Fermentation_Condition: Agar plugs of CR252M were initially grown at 25 °C on yeast malt agar plates supplemented with 30 μg/mL streptomycin and 12 μg/mL chlortetracycline. After one week, 3 macerated agar plugs from this plate were placed in 75 mL media [potato dextrose broth (24 g/L)] in a 125 mL erlenmeyer at a pH of 6.1. It was grown at 28 °C and 150 rpm for 6 days. Then the grains of barley (200 g) and wheat (200 g) were ground with the aid of a mixer and subsequently the rest of components [1 mL of magnesium chloride (20 mg/mL solution stock), 2 g of peptone, and 250 mL of distilled water] were added. The flasks containing 24.4 g of solid media, each, were autoclaved for 30 min at 121 °C. Each flask was inoculated with 15 mL of seed medium; and it was incubated at 25 °C for 21 days.

Plant_Material: CR 1207B was isolated from the petiole of Geonoma hoffmanniana, in the summit of Cacao Volcano in October, 2006 (collection permit R-CM-INBio-03-2006-OT).
Fermentation_Condition: Agar plugs of CR1207B were initially grown at 25 °C on yeast malt agar plates supplemented with 30 μg/mL streptomycin and 12 μg/mL chlortetracycline. After one week, agar plugs from this plate were placed in 75 mL of rich seed media [5 g peptone, 10 g dextrose, 3 g yeast extract, 10 g malt extract per 1 L water (pH 6.2)] in a 125 mL Erlenmeyer at a pH of 6.2. They were grown at 25 °C and 150 rpm for 6 days. 150 mL of 0.66% (w/v) malt extract and 5 g HP-20 resin were then added to each flask with 15 mL of the seed media in a 250 mL erlenmeyer, and the fungi were cultured under the same conditions for 16 days. The fungal cultures were then incubated at 25 °C without shaking for 5 days.

Plant_Material: The endophytic fungus Eurotium cristatum EN-220 was isolated, by using of a standard procedure as described in our previous report, from the marine alga Sargassum thunbergii collected from Huiquan bay in Qingdao, P. R. China.
Fermentation_Condition: For chemical investigations, the fungal strain was statically fermented at r.t. for 30 days on sterilized solid medium containing rice (100 g/flask), peptone (0.6 g/flask), and sea water (100 mL/flask) in 1-1 Fernbach flasks (×100).

Plant_Material: The producing strain Streptomyces sp. neau50 was isolated from healthy soybean root in Harbin, Heilongjiang province, China.
Fermentation_Condition: The strain Streptomyces sp. neau50 was maintained on the medium containing glucose 10 g, maltose 3 g, yeast extract 3 g, K2HPO43H2O 0.5 g, MgSO47H2O 0.5 g, NaCl 0.5 g, KNO3 1 g and agar 20 g in 1.0 L tap water, pH 7.0. The seed medium consisted of glucose 4 g, maltodextrin 10 g, yeast extract 4 g, CaCO3 2 g in 1.0 L water and pH 7.2–7.4. All the media were sterilized at 121 C for 20 min. Slant culture was incubated for 6–7 days at 28 C. Fermentation was carried out in 50 L first seed fermentor (containing 30 L fermentation broth), 500 L second fermentor (containing 300 L fermentation broth) successively. The producing medium was composed of glucose 1%, soluble amylum 4%, yeast extract 0.5%, soybean powder 2.5%, peptone 0.5%, CaCO3 0.2%, MgSO47H2O 0.8%, FeSO47H2O 0.6%, ZnSO47H2O 0.2%, MnSO4H2O 0.2%, CoCl26H2O 0.05%, Na2MoO42H2O 0.2%, and pH 7.0 before sterilization. The fermentation was conducted at 28 C for 7 days stirred at 100 r min1 with an aeration rate of 30 m3 of air per hour.

Plant_Material: The fungal strain A729 was isolated from the fresh branches of the medicinal plant Morinda officinalis, which was collected in January 2015.
Fermentation_Condition: The endophytic fungus Trichoderma koningiopsis A729 was cultivated in potato dextrose broth (potato 20%, glucose 2%, K2HPO4 0.3%, MgSO4.7H2O 0.15%, vitamin B 10 mg/L) at 28 °C for 7 days to prepare the seed culture. Then, the inoculated seed culture was transferred into each of a total of 100 flasks (1000 mL) containing 500 mL of potato dextrose broth. The liquid cultivation was then kept for 7 days at 28 °C and 120 r/m on a rotary shaker.

After autoclaving at 121 °C for 20 min and then cooling to room temperature, each flask was inoculated and then incubated at 28 °C under static conditions. After 30 days, the fermentation was stopped by adding 500 mL of EtOAc to each flask.

Plant_Material: The green algae, Halimeda opuntia collected from the Egyptian Red Sea site at a depth of 5-8 m from the coast of Rass Mohamed (south Sinai, Egypt) in March 2010.
Fermentation_Condition: Stock cultures of the fungus, was used to inoculate 500 mL of liquid medium in an Erlenmeyer flask (3 L) containing biomalt broth in 50% seawater. It was then cultured at 35 ± 2 ℃ on a rotary shaker at 200 rpm. The flask was incubated for 72 h and used as first stage inoculums. The same medium (10 L) was made in 75 Erlenmayer flasks (1 L) and inoculated with 5% of first stage inoculums. The flasks were incubated statically for 15 days at 35 ℃.

It was then cultured at 35 ± 2 ℃ on a rotary shaker at 200 rpm. The flask was incubated for 72 h and used as first stage inoculums. The same medium (10 L) was made in 75 Erlenmayer flasks (1 L) and inoculated with 5% of first stage inoculums. The flasks were incubated statically for 15 days at 35 ℃.

Fermentation_Condition: A 2.5 cm wide strip of agar was removed from the mid-portion of a standard PDA Petri dish, then M. albus was inoculated and grown on one side of the plate for varying time periods prior to testing. Plant_Material: These sterile odoriferous fungi only appeared in plants obtained from the Northern Territory of Australia and not those from Tasmania. Furthermore, only Grevillea pterifolia (collected at 13° 07′ 947″ S, 132° 27′ 435″ E), Kennedia nigriscans (collected at 12° 57′ 991″ S, 132° 48′ 818″ E) and Terminalia prostrata (12° 12′ 137″ S, 132° 47′ 066″ E) yielded such sterile odoriferous fungi.
Fermentation_Condition: Potato dextrose agar (PDA) was poured into all quadrants of commercially available Petri plates with the base half-plate separated into quadrants. Then, into one quadrant, a small plug of agar containing an actively growing culture of the tested isolate was placed. The plate was sealed and incubated for 4 days at 23 °C prior to exposure of the test fungi and bacteria to the VOCs of the M. albus isolate arising in the plates. Individual fungi were inoculated in the plate on a 3 mm×3 mm×3 mm plug of agar. Bacteria and Saccharomyces cerevisiae were streaked (1.5 cm streaks) on to the other quadrants of the plate, one organism in each quadrant. The dividing walls in the plate precluded the diffusion of any inhibitory soluble compounds emanating from the M. albus isolate to the organisms being tested. The plate was wrapped with two pieces of Parafilm and incubated at 23 °C.

Plant_Material: The fungal strain Hypoxylon investiens was isolated from the stems of Litsea akoensis var. chitouchiaoensis, collected in Wutai, Pingtung County, Taiwan, during July of 2011.
Fermentation_Condition: Seven-day-old colonies of the H. investiens strain on potato dextrose agar (PDA) medium in 9-cm Petri dish were cut into the bottle and blended for 30 s with 100 ml of dist. H2O to prepare the fungal inoculum for liquid fermentation. To each 500-ml flask containing 150 ml of liquid cultural media (ingredients: corn starch, 30 g; corn steep liquor, 10 g; yeast extract, 5 g; and sea salt, 2 g in 1 l of dist. H2O, pH 6) were added 10 ml of fungal inocula and incubated at 258 for 3 weeks on a rotary shaker at the speed of 150 circles/min.

Plant_Material: Endophytic fungi from Costa Rica.
Fermentation_Condition: Agar plugs of CR237A and CR1092F were initially grown at 25°C on yeast malt agar plates supplemented with 30 μg/ml streptomycin and 12 μg/ml chlortetracycline. After one week, agar plugs of this plate were placed in 150 ml of rich seed media in 1 L flasks. They were grown at 25 °C and 150 rpm for 7 days. 450 ml of 0.66% (w/v) malt extract and 10 g HP-20 resin were then added to each flask, and the fungi were cultured under the same conditions for 21 days. The fungal cultures were then held at 25 °C without shaking for 5 days.

Plant_Material: Healthy leaf samples of Albizia lebbeck (L.) Benth. were collected from the Jammu (32°43′58″N, 74°48′32″E) region of Jammu and Kashmir, India during August 2014.
Fermentation_Condition: The endophytic fungal strain was subcultured on PDA media incubated at 28°C for 7 days. Five agar plugs of approximately 2 mm2 were taken to inoculate 500 ml Erlenmeyer flasks containing 150 ml of sterile potato dextrose broth (PDB), incubated at 28 ± 2°C for 2 days in the dark in an incubator shaker at 150 rev min−1 to obtain the seed culture. Thirty milliltres of seed culture was used to inoculate 1 l Erlenmeyer flasks each containing 300 ml of PDB and incubated for 10 days under the same conditions as the seed culture.

Five agar plugs of approximately 2 mm2 were taken to inoculate 500 ml Erlenmeyer flasks containing 150 ml of sterile potato dextrose broth (PDB), incubated at 28 ± 2°C for 2 days in the dark in an incubator shaker at 150 rev min−1 to obtain the seed culture. Thirty milliltres of seed culture was used to inoculate 1 l Erlenmeyer flasks each containing 300 ml of PDB and incubated for 10 days under the same conditions as the seed culture.

Plant_Material: P. pseudosydowianum was obtained by isolation of a single ascospore, using a Skerman micromanipulator, from the petiole of Quercus crispula var. crispula in Yoshiwa, Hatsukaichi, Hiroshima prefecture, in September 2013.
Fermentation_Condition: P. pseudosydowianum was inoculated in 100 mL Erlenmeyer flasks (×10), each containing 30 mL of the seed medium (PYG: 20 g of glucose, 10 g of polypeptone, 5 g of yeast extract, and 1 L of deionized water; the pH was adjusted to 7.5 with 1 N NaOH before autoclaving). After incubation on a rotary shaker at 120 rpm, 24.5°C for 11 d, each seed culture was transferred into 500 mL Erlenmeyer shaking flasks (×20), each containing 100 mL of PYG medium and incubated on a rotary shaker at 190 rpm, 24.5°C for 1 week.

Plant_Material: Healthy root of Panax ginseng was collected in Changchun, Jilin Province, People’s Republic of China.
Fermentation_Condition: The endophytic fungi were initially grown on a PDA medium in Petri dishes and then transferred into shake flasks culture by punching out 5 mm of the agar plate culture using a self-designed cutter. The shake flask culture (250 ml) was carried out containing 100 ml potato dextrose broth medium at 26 °C, 180 rpm for 7 days and then transferred into 5-L Erlenmeyer flasks. About 60 L of fermentation liquid was obtained after incubation under the same condition for 10 days. The mycelial pellets were harvested by filtration and then thoroughly crushed in a mortar.

Plant_Material: The fungus Cladosporium sphaerospermum WBS017 was isolated from healthy bulbs of Fritillaria unibracteata var. wabuensis.
Fermentation_Condition: Twenty-three 1 L Erlenmeyer flasks with solid rice medium (100 g of rice and 100 mL of demineralized water for each one) were used for a large-scale fermentation. They were autoclaved at 121 °C for 20 min and cooled to room temperature, followed by inoculation and cultivation of the fungus under static conditions. When the fungus had completely overgrown the medium, EtOAc (600 mL) was added to each flask to stop cultivation. After cutting the fermentation medium into small pieces, the flasks were shaken at 150 rpm for half a day.

Plant_Material: Healthy stems from several Cinnamomum camphora plants growing in a field at Nanjing University, Jiangsu, China were sampled in February 2005.
Fermentation_Condition: The strain LCH001 was further transferred to 4 ml of PS liquid media in a 15-ml tube and incubated in shake flasks running at 100 rpm and held at 30 °C for 2 days. After removal of the endophytic cells by centrifugation of the culture broth at 4,000 rpm for 30 min and then 0.22 μm filtration, 1 ml of the filtrate mixed with 9 ml of the PSA medium containing ampicillin sodium (400 μg/ml) were poured into a Petri dish (9 cm in diameter). Once the medium had cooled, 5 discs (7 mm in diameter), 1 from each of the target fungi, taken from the fresh margin of the mycelium, were spaced out equally on the Petri dish, and the dish was incubated at 30 °C for 48 h.

Fermentation_Condition: The hypha with PDA pieces (approximately 4 mm × 4 mm) were inoculated into 60 mL PDB culture medium in culture flask for incubation at 120 rpm and 20 to 25°C for 4 days. Plant_Material: Healthy leaves of P. fruticosa were collected in January 2017 from Mae Chan District, Chiang Rai Province, Thailand (99°70′56″E, 20°10′36″N) for endophytic fungi isolation.

Plant_Material: The leaves and stem of Boswellia sacra from wild and domestic trees were selected for the isolation of endophytic fungi.
Fermentation_Condition: Czapek broth was used for the isolation of secondary metabolites. The ingredients and their amounts for the preparation of Czapek broth included; glucose 1%, peptone 1%, KCl 0.05%, MgSO4.7H2O 0.05%, and FeSO4.7H2O 0.001% for 4.5 liters. The pH was kept at about 7.3 ± 0.2; at 28 °C and grown for 21 days in a shaking incubator at 120 rpm.

Plant_Material: The marine fungus A terreus C23-3 (GDMCC No. 60316) was collected from the coral Pectinia paeonia in the Xuwen Coral Reserve of Zhanjiang.
Fermentation_Condition: The producer strain was activated and cultured on a potato sucrose peptone agar (PSPA) petri dish at 28 °C for seven days. The spore suspension was collected to inoculate 3 L-flasks, each containing 1 L autoclaved potato sucrose peptone broth medium containing 200 mL potato juice per L from 200 g fresh potato, sucrose 20 g/L, peptone 5 g/L, and sea salt 20 g/L, ZnCl2 10 mM, with pH 7.2 ± 0.2. The fungus was statically cultured for 28 days.

Plant_Material: The rhizome of Zingiber officinale Rosc. var. athira was collected from Kerala Agricultural University, Thrissur, Kerala.
Fermentation_Condition: Large-scale fermentation of the isolate was done on solid rice media. Plant_Material: Fruit bodies of Shiraia bambusicola were collected from Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China and those of Rubroshiraia bambusae from Yulong County, Yunnan, China.
Fermentation_Condition: The endophytic fungi isolates were cultured on PDA at 26 °C for 7 days. Based on colony colour, three strains representing different morphs were selected for further experiments. Five plugs (5 mm in diameter) of growing culture plus the adhering mycelium were added to 250 mL Erlenmeyer flasks containing 150 mL of Potato Dextrose Broth media (PDB, containing 200 g/L potato and 20 g/L dextrose). All liquid cultures were kept at 26 °C for 10 d with shaking (180 rpm).

Plant_Material: Dicoma anomala plant material was collected in April 2018 from the natural habitat with slit soil type in Eisleben, Limpopo province, South Africa (23.52 S 29.824 E).
Fermentation_Condition: The bacterial endophytes were cultured in 1L Luria Broth (LB) for 7 days at 28°C on a shaking incubator at 180 rpm. After cultivation, 2 g/L of sterilized Amberlite® XAD-7-HP resin (Sigma-Aldrich, Darmstadt, Germany) was added to the cultures and shaken for 2 hours at 180 rpm, to absorb the secondary metabolites.

Plant_Material: Endophytic fungal strains were isolated from Smallanthus sonchifolius (Asteraceae).
Fermentation_Condition: To carry out the single culture, fungal strains were cultured individually in 500 ml Erlenmeyer flasks containing 200 ml of malt extract medium (7 g malt extract in 1 l distilled water) at 30 °C on an orbital shaker at 150 rpm for 14 days. To establish fermentative growth, each flask was inoculated with 10 ml of a pure 7-day fungal pre-culture. The pre-cultures were prepared by transferring 3 plugs of 5 mm diam from the fungal colonies grown in potato dextrose agar (PDA) into a rich medium (5 g tryptone, 10 g dextrose, 3 g yeast extract, and 10 g malt extract in 1 l distilled water). The dual mixed culture was initiated by combining the pre-cultures of each fungus in one flask of fermentative liquid medium. The cultures were extracted using bags containing 10 g of diaion HP-20 resin that were added to the medium during the 7th day of fermentative growth. After 7 additional days, the resin was extracted with acetone and ethanol, and the extracts were dried under vacuum.

Plant_Material: The producing organism was isolated from surface-sterilized tissue of Artemisia annua collected from Xishuangbanna, Yunnan province, China.
Fermentation_Condition: A slant culture of the strain was inoculated into 500 ml Erlenmeyer flasks containing 100 ml of seed medium composed of yeast extract 0.4%, glucose 0.4%, malt extract 0.5%, multiple vitamins solution 0.35 ml l−1, pH 7.2 with no adjustment and cultured for 2 days at 28 °C on a rotary shaker at 220 r.p.m. This seed culture was used to inoculate the fermentation medium with 10% volume. The fermentation was carried out in 1000 ml Erlenmeyer flasks containing 300 ml of fermentation medium containing starch 2.4%, beef extract 0.3%, glucose 0.1%, yeast extract 0.5%, peptone 0.3%, CaCO3 0.4% at pH 7.0 with no adjustment and cultured for 7 days at 28 °C on a rotary shaker at 220 r.p.m. for upscale fermentation.

All NA plates were maintained in 25 °C for 6 d until the creation of a clear inhibition zone between the fungus and strain Cal.l.30.

Plant_Material: Plant tissues (fresh leaves, stems, and seeds) were collected from matured adlay in September 2010 in a hilly region of Taishun County in the Zhejiang Province in China.
Fermentation_Condition: All endophytic fungi obtained were inoculated into 250-mL erlenmeyer flasks containing 100 mL rice medium. Biomass of endophytic fungi was removed by filtration after incubation for 10 days at 28° on an incubatory shaker at 180 rpm; the mycelia and broth were treated separately.

Plant_Material: Leaves of Passiflora incarnata were randomly sampled from mature, healthy-looking plants grown in the Centroflora Group agricultural fields, Botucatu, São Paulo, Brazil (22°56′18.40"S, 48°34′04.20"W).
Fermentation_Condition: The isolates were cultured for seven days in PDA medium plates and after this period, four to five 0.5 cm agar discs containing mycelium were inoculated in 250 mL Erlenmeyer flasks for fermentation with 100 mL of potato dextrose broth. The flasks were incubated at 28 ℃, under shaking condition (120 rpm). After 15 days, the fermented broth was filtered by Whatman No. 1 filter paper.

Plant_Material: The endophytic fungus Aspergillus flavus L7 was isolated in pure culture from the leaf tissue of Aegle marmelos obtained from the Toranmal forest of Nandurbar district of India.
Fermentation_Condition: Isolated fungal strains were cultivated at shake flask level. All the isolates were inoculated in 50 ml sterile seed medium (CzapekDox broth) to prepare inoculum. After development of sufficient biomass, 10 % inoculum was aseptically transferred to 500-ml Erlenmeyer flask containing 150 ml sterile Czapek Dox broth (pH 5.0). Fermentation was carried out on rotary shaker at 120 rpm for 20 days.
Extract_Activity: Anti-bacterial activity; Anti-fungal activity; Anti-oxidant activity

Plant_Material: The endophytic fungus Dzf12 was isolated from the healthy rhizomes of Dioscorea zingiberensis collected in Hubei Province in June 2011.
Fermentation_Condition: The endophytic fungus was cultured on PDA (potato 200 g/L, dextrose 20 g/L, and agar 20 g/L) medium in Petri dishes at 25 °C for 10 days. After 7 days, the fungal cultures were harvested.

Then, three agar plugs (0.5 × 0.5 cm) were inoculated in a 1000 mL Erlenmeyer flask containing 300 mL of potato dextrose broth (potato 200 g/L and dextrose 20 g/L) medium and incubated on a rotary shaker at 150 rpm and 25 °C for 7 days. After 7 days, the fungal cultures were harvested.

Plant_Material: Mature, healthy and disease-free leaf samples of the medicinally important plant Euphorbia hirta were collected randomly from the Botanical Garden, Banaras Hindu University (BHU) Varanasi, India.
Fermentation_Condition: Mycelial disc (5 mm) of freshly grown endophytic EHL2 was cultured in 500-ml Erlenmeyer flasks, each containing 200 ml of different media. All the five different culture media (Himedia), i.e. potato dextrose broth (PDB), Czapek Dox broth (CDB), Czapek Dox yeast extract broth (CDYEB), malt extract broth (MEB) and Sabouraud dextrose broth (SDB), were adopted for fermentation and incubated at 26 ± 2 °C. After 21 days of incubation, mycelia of all the cultures were filtered through muslin cloth.

Plant_Material: The endophytes were isolated from medicinal plant ‘Glycyrrhiza glabra’ collected from Kashmir Himalayas (located between 34°5′N and 74°47′E at an elevation of around 1585 m) of Jammu and Kashmir State, India.
Fermentation_Condition: The strain was subjected to large-scale fermentation in potato dextrose liquid medium for a period of 10 days at 28 ± 2°C in a shaking incubator (180 rpm; New Brunswick's, Innova 4200). Starting materials for fermentation experiments were taken from an actively growing stock culture, which were sub-cultured on fresh slants and incubated for 7 days at pH 7.0 and temperature 28°C. After 10 days, culture broth was centrifuged followed by addition of ethyl acetate (HPLC grade) equal to the volume of cell homogenate for its extraction and ethyl acetate layer was separated.

Plant_Material: The endophytic actinomycete strain SKH1-2, which exhibited a high antimicrobial activity, was isolated from roots of Musa (ABB) cv. ‘Kluai Sao Kratuep Ho’ collected in Suphan Buri province (14° 54′ 22.5″ N/100° 04′ 50″ E), Thailand, from June to August 2015.
Fermentation_Condition: An endophytic actinomycete strain SKH1-2 was grown and maintained on ISP 2 agar slant. A loopful of cells of strain SKH1-2 was inoculated into a test tube containing 10 mL of the seed medium (2.4% starch, 0.1% glucose, 0.3% peptone, 0.3% meat extract, 0.5% yeast extract and 0.3% CaCO3, pH 7.0). The tubes were cultivated on a rotary shaker (200 rpm) at 28 °C for 4 days. Afterwards, a 1 mL portion of the first seed culture was transferred into a 500-mL Erlenmeyer flask containing 100 mL of the seed medium and incubated at the same condition as described above. For production, a 1 mL portion of the second inoculum was transferred to 500-mL Erlenmeyer flasks (total 60 flasks), each containing 100 mL of the medium 51 (0.5% glucose, 0.5% corn steep powder, 1% oat meal, 1% defatted cotton seed powder, 0.5% K2HPO4, 0.5% MgSO4.7H2O and 1 mL/L of trace metal solution, pH 7.0), at 28 °C, 200 rpm for 7 days. Trace metal solution contained each 1.0 g/L of FeSO4.7H2O, MnCl2.4H2O, ZnSO4.7H2O, CuSO4.5H2O and CoCl2.6H2O. The production culture was carried out on rotary shakers (200 rpm) for 6 days at 28 °C.

Fermentation_Condition: The rice medium was prepared in Erlenmeyer flasks (500 mL) containing 50 g of rice and 90 mL of ultra-pure water followed by sterilization (121 °C, 20 min). After 5 days of incubation in PDB 5 mL was transferred to rice for solid incubation at 28 °C under static conditions. After 28 days both fermentations, in rice and PDB, were stopped by adding 200 mL of EtOAc to an Erlenmeyer flask and 20 min in an ultrasonic bath.

Plant_Material: The producer strain CF-298113 was isolated from surface disinfected root pieces of Triticum sp. collected in a traditional agricultural land in Montefrío (Granada, Spain).
Fermentation_Condition: Strain CF-298113 was fermented by inoculating 10 mycelial agar plugs into SMYA medium (Bacto neopeptone 10 g; maltose 40 g; yeast extract 10 g; agar 3 g; H2O 1 L) in two flasks (50 mL of medium in a 250-mL Erlenmeyer). The flasks were incubated on a rotary shaker at 220 rpm at 22 °C with 70% relative humidity. After growing the seed stage for 7 days, aliquots of 4 mL were used to inoculate 20 × 500-mL Erlenmeyer flasks containing the production solid rice-based medium (BRFT). The BRFT medium contained 20 g of brown rice and 40 mL of a solution of yeast extract 1 g/L, sodium tartrate 0.5 g/L and KH2PO4 0.5 g/L per flask. The 20 flasks seeded were incubated under static conditions at 22 °C and 70% relative humidity for 21 days.

Plant_Material: The green healthy mature leaves of T. arjuna were collected from the Botany Field Research and Herbal Science Center, University of Madras, Chennai (formerly Madras), Southern India.
Fermentation_Condition: The endophytic fungus was grown in 2-litre Erlenmeyer flasks containing 500 ml of MID medium supplemented with 1 g of Soytone l-1 and incubated for 21 days. The mixture was incubated for 14 days in the dark at 28 °C.

Fermentation_Condition: The strain Y3111 was cultivated on ISP2 agar plates at 28 °C for 7 days. A 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask pre-culture of Y3111, containing 50 mL of M001 medium, was inoculated and incubated with pieces of well-grown agar cultures of the strain at 28 °C (220 rpm) for 48 h. The pre-culture was used to inoculate ten 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask (each with 5 mL of pre-culture and 100 mL M001 medium) and incubated at 28 °C (220 rpm) for 3 days to obtain seed cultures for large-scaled fermentation. Each of the seed cultures was aseptically transferred to 80 250 mL Erlenmeyer flasks containing 100 mL of M001 medium and 5 g of HP20 resin and was harvested after 5 days incubation at 28 °C 220 rpm.
